evidence.note: 'About 40% of what flats on blocks C and D spend on electricity falls in daylight hours': a specific declarative finding, one sentence, no trailing full stop, no italics.
'26 of the 33 households that answered the survey support a pilot' states the finding and matches the evidence; the respondents-vs-all-households caveat sits in the reader note, as the profile asks.
Resident quote presented verbatim under a neutral label ('Resident, block D') with no editorialising.
'Heavy daytime users get the largest credit.' and the caption 'Blocks C and D each get their own array.' are plain cause-to-consequence sentences; no hooks or epigram closers anywhere in the deck.
Risk bullets are short and concrete ('Upkeep after year five: £1,150 a year'); disputed payback shown as installer vs treasurer without framing; notes flag 'Single-sourced' and 'Disputed' plainly.
'The board is asked to approve the £86,400 pilot, with a go or stop review at twelve months' reads as a procedural request rather than a finding; a minor lapse the presenter might reword.
'We propose a 12-month pilot on two roofs.' is plain and direct; byline follows the '<name>, <Month year>' pattern.

rationale: Titles are complete, specific declarative findings, body copy explains mechanism plainly, the quote is verbatim, and there are no aphorisms, antitheses or hooks. The only lapse is the s-7 title, which states an ask rather than a finding. That fits level 4.
